title: Epic — Silkweb v1: rebuild MWeb core with real folder structuring
description:
## Summary

Silkweb is a clean-room native macOS offline Markdown library and editor (macOS 15+, SwiftUI + AppKit) that rebuilds MWeb’s core writing experience while fixing the main gap: **one unified library where nested folders on disk own documents** (UTF-8 `.md`), with tags/search/editing in one place—not separate category DB vs Folders modes.

This epic tracks the **Core v1** sequence from `research.md` (2026-10-01): durable storage and folder mutations first, then shell and editing, preview/rendering, search/tags, export, and polish. The repo today is a skeleton (version constant + placeholder window); no feature code to preserve.

**Principles:** offline-first, no accounts/backend; atomic saves; macOS Trash for deletion; versioned tolerant JSON metadata; performance targets 10k docs / 1k folders with work off the main thread; keyboard-friendly native Mac UX.

**Build/test gate:** `./scripts/build.sh` and `./scripts/build.sh test` per issue; no bare `swift build`. QA PASS + Orchestrator approval closes issues on `team/roadmap`.

**Existing open issues:** None at research time (no prior `.beads`); no duplicates noted.

## Open questions (defaults apply until answered)

1. Is the pain specifically MWeb Library categories, or a failing operation in its Folders window? The proposed unified model addresses the former without falsely claiming MWeb lacks the latter.
2. Is the proposed Core release sufficient without math/Mermaid, full CommonMark conformance, tabs, focus/typewriter and DOCX/ePub? Which is a daily necessity?
3. Should the initial library open an existing directory in place by default, or start with a new folder and offer Import Copy? Both should remain explicit.
4. Are sidecar tags acceptable, or must tags travel inside Markdown front matter? The proposal avoids altering document text; a portable front-matter contract is separate scope.
5. Confirm system Trash plus Finder restoration for v1, direct folder counts, and name/date sorting without manual order.
6. Is migration via MWeb's own Markdown folder export sufficient? Multiple category memberships can become duplicate exported files; automated DB migration would require a separate clean-room specification.
7. Does switching to standard Cmd-O and Cmd-Shift-O matter more than copying MWeb's contextual Cmd-O behavior?

## Out of scope for this epic

Follow-up issues required (not in the 25 Core tickets): **Math**, **Mermaid**, **full CommonMark conformance**, **tabs/session**, **focus/typewriter**, **backups/history UI**, **HTML paste conversion**, **TextBundle**, **rich text copy**, **DOCX**, and **ePub**. Also excluded: online publishing, image hosting, static-site generation, CloudKit/sync, mobile apps, script/Pandoc auto-execution, manual document ordering on disk, scroll-synced preview, backlink browser, Quick Note, pin/unpin, and proprietary MWeb image-width syntax as default.

No third-party dependency is silently assumed; math/diagrams need explicitly scoped follow-ups with approved dependencies.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.text: PRODUCT OWNER DECISIONS (2026-10-01): (1) v1 scope ADDS Tabs/sessions and Focus/typewriter mode as their own tickets; math, Mermaid, DOCX/ePub etc. stay Later. (2) Tags are stored in the Silkweb sidecar index (.silkweb metadata) — never written into .md text/front matter. (3) First launch offers BOTH 'Open folder in place' and 'New library'; 'Import Copy' lives in the File menu.

title: #1 Disk library model and tolerant metadata
description:
**Roadmap #:** 1 · **Scope:** L · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
Notes need a durable, tool-independent home on disk.

### Proposed behavior
Enumerate one library root into folder/document models off the main thread; UTF-8 reads; stable app IDs; versioned JSON with tolerant decode and rebuildable derived index; no implicit symlink traversal.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Library files plus category database (Silkweb: real folders + `.md` + versioned JSON index).

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/LibraryModels.swift, LibraryScanner.swift, LibraryMetadata.swift; Tests/SilkwebCoreTests/LibraryScannerTests.swift (or similar).

### Constraints
Persistence: version JSON; missing keys default safely; bodies stay in `.md` only. Performance: enumeration off main thread; target 10k/1k synthetic tree.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] `./scripts/build.sh` succeeds
- [x] `./scripts/build.sh test` passes with new XCTest coverage for the scanner and metadata (e.g. `LibraryScannerTests`, `LibraryMetadataTests`)
- [x] Metadata JSON carries a format version; a metadata file missing optional keys (simulating an older version) and a missing metadata file both load with defaults
- [x] Nested and empty folders appear in the scanned model; only `.md`/`.markdown` files become documents; hidden files and the `.silkweb` metadata dir are excluded
- [x] Malformed metadata JSON does not crash: it is set aside (not deleted) and the derived index is rebuilt from disk
- [x] Symlinks are not followed implicitly; a symlink cycle in a fixture does not hang the scan
- [x] Synthetic 10,000-document / 1,000-folder tree enumerates off the main thread within a stated budget measured in a test
close_reason: QA PASS attempt 1: build + 11/11 tests (orchestrator re-ran: green). Scanner/metadata: versioned tolerant JSON, malformed index set aside + rebuilt, symlink cycles skipped, 10k/1k synthetic tree in 0.27s off-main. Read-only-root write issue carried to silkweb-1.4 as a comment.

comments.author: engineer
comments.text: Implemented Core async disk scanner, folder/document snapshot, strict UTF-8 reads, and atomic version-1 path-to-ID metadata. IDs persist across rescans; external move reconciliation remains #11. Corrupt metadata is preserved as index.corrupt-<UUID>.json before rebuilding; newer formats and metadata symlinks fail without overwriting. Validation: ./scripts/build.sh succeeds; ./scripts/build.sh test passes all 11 tests. 10,000-document / 1,000-folder scan measured 0.280985s against a 10s budget, called on main actor with worker main-thread precondition. Standalone Swift self-test in $TMPDIR passed 40 extension/hidden/nesting/empty-content combinations, 4 metadata key combinations, invalid UTF-8, traversal rejection, and symlink-root rejection. No design notes or issue comments were present. All acceptance boxes checked; left in_progress for QA and Orchestrator.

comments.author: qa
comments.text: QA PASS: build + 11 tests pass; reviewed diff against all 7 criteria (versioned tolerant metadata, nested/empty folders, md/markdown filter, hidden/.silkweb excluded, corrupt JSON backed up + rebuilt, symlink/cycle skipped, 10k/1k scan ~0.27s off-main vs 10s budget). Non-blocking note: scan always rewrites index.json, so a read-only library root fails the scan.

### MWeb / competitor reference

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/MarkdownParser.swift, MarkdownAST.swift, HTMLRenderer.swift; fixture tests.

No document scripts; no network loads from renderer.

title: #26 Document tabs and session restore
description:
**Scope:** L · **Priority:** P2 · **Product-owner request (2026-10-01)**

### User problem
The three-pane shell (#4) and single-document editor (#5) cannot keep multiple notes open, reuse a preview slot, or restore the last working set after quit—unlike MWeb’s tabbed editor workflow (`research.md` **Tabs/session**).

### Proposed behavior
- **Tab bar** in the editor pane of the main window: each tab binds one library document (stable ID from #1) with its own dirty buffer via `DocumentSession` / save coordinator (#3, #5).
- **Preview vs pinned:** one replaceable *preview* tab; selecting a document in the list opens it there unless that document is already open in another tab. First edit or double-click *fixes* the tab (pinned); pinned tabs persist across list selections until closed.
- **Tab chrome:** reorder (drag), close, **Close Others**, **Close Tabs to the Right**; **Cmd-W** closes the active tab (not the window when tabs remain—align with standard Mac tab semantics).
- **Navigation:** **Ctrl-Tab** and **Cmd-Shift-]** activate next tab (document shortcut collision matrix in #25; do not steal Cmd-R preview toggle, Cmd-O / Cmd-Shift-O open paths from #20, or find/replace keys from #13).
- **Session restore:** on launch, restore open tabs (pinned + preview state), active tab, and selected folder from versioned library/window metadata; decode tolerantly; drop entries whose files are missing; when a file was moved externally, rebind tab to the same stable document ID via library reconcile (#11) / move IDs (#7) when possible.
- **Moves:** when #7 moves or renames a document, open tabs follow the file path without orphan buffers.
- **Quit/close:** save coordinator flushes every dirty tab before tab close, window close, and app termination.

### MWeb / competitor reference
`research.md` **Tabs/session** (H/L2): replaceable preview tab; editing or double-click makes tab fixed; reorder/close subsets; reopen last session.

### Likely files
Sources/Silkweb/EditorTabBar.swift, TabbedEditorPane.swift, LibraryWorkspace.swift (list → tab routing), DocumentSession.swift, AppCommands.swift; Sources/SilkwebCore/WindowSessionMetadata.swift (or extend LibraryMetadata.swift) with tolerant Codable + tests in Tests/SilkwebCoreTests/WindowSessionMetadataTests.swift.

### Constraints
- Repo today is skeleton-only (`SilkwebApp.swift` placeholder; no tab or shortcut code yet)—implement on top of #4/#5 deliverables.
- Follow #5 autosave/debounce and flush-before-close; follow #7 move/link semantics for open documents.
- Session JSON must version and default missing keys; never block launch on stale session data.
- No per-keystroke library rescan (AGENTS.md performance rules).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `./scripts/build.sh` succeeds
- [ ] `./scripts/build.sh test` passes with new XCTest coverage for session metadata encode/decode (missing files, tolerant defaults, stable-ID rebind)
- [ ] List selection opens document in preview tab; editing or double-click pins; selecting another doc replaces preview only
- [ ] Reorder, close, Close Others, and Close Tabs to the Right behave on mixed pinned/preview tabs
- [ ] Cmd-W closes active tab; Ctrl-Tab and Cmd-Shift-] cycle tabs without conflicting with documented shortcuts from #13/#18/#20
- [ ] Quit and tab close flush dirty buffers via save coordinator (#3/#5); failed save keeps tab open with buffer intact
- [ ] After relaunch, tabs, active tab, and selected folder restore; entries for deleted files are dropped silently; moved files reattach when ID resolves (#7/#11)
- [ ] Files saved before this change still load (library documents and pre-tab metadata unchanged)

title: #27 Focus and typewriter writing modes
description:
**Scope:** M · **Priority:** P2 · **Product-owner request (2026-10-01)**

### User problem
Long-form writing in the source editor lacks distraction-reducing view modes MWeb exposes in preferences (`research.md` **Focus/typewriter**): a focus dimming mode and typewriter-style vertical caret anchoring.

### Proposed behavior
- **View menu** toggles (per window, checkable): **Focus Mode** and **Typewriter Mode**; states persist in user preferences and restore per window where applicable.
- **Focus:** dim all text except the active **paragraph** (default) or **sentence**—granularity is a setting added to the writing preferences model alongside #24 fields.
- **Typewriter:** keep the caret line at a fixed vertical position (default: vertical center of the visible editor) while typing/scrolling; works together with Focus.
- **Rendering:** dimming composes with incremental Markdown styling attributes from #12 (no full-buffer syntax pass); update only visible range / affected paragraphs on caret or edit notifications—no per-keystroke whole-document work (AGENTS.md).
- **Settings UI:** extend the #24 settings scene with Focus granularity and typewriter vertical anchor (and any threshold slider if needed); defaults documented and tolerant on decode.

### MWeb / competitor reference
`research.md` **Focus/typewriter** (L2): focus toggle and typewriter scrolling-threshold preference; exact MWeb dimming curve unverified—match readable contrast, not pixel parity.

### Likely files
Sources/Silkweb/MarkdownTextView.swift (visible-range attribute updates, scroll anchoring), FocusTypewriterController.swift; Sources/SilkwebCore/WritingPreferences.swift (new keys); Sources/Silkweb/SettingsView.swift (additional rows); AppCommands.swift (View menu); Tests/SilkwebCoreTests/WritingPreferencesTests.swift (defaults/bounds).

### Constraints
- Depends on #12 so formatting attributes and IME/undo grouping remain correct when dimming.
- Depends on #24 for preference persistence and settings shell—this ticket adds keys + UI rows rather than expanding #24’s original acceptance scope.
- Keyboard shortcuts for toggles defer to #25 integration pass except where needed for basic menu validation; do not collide with tab shortcuts from the tabs ticket.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `./scripts/build.sh` succeeds
- [ ] `./scripts/build.sh test` passes with new XCTest coverage for WritingPreferences focus/typewriter keys and defaults
- [ ] View menu toggles Focus and Typewriter per window; states persist across relaunch
- [ ] Focus dims non-active paragraph or sentence per setting; active region remains full contrast with #12 styling intact
- [ ] Typewriter mode keeps caret line at configured vertical anchor (default center) while typing in a long document
- [ ] Focus and Typewriter can be enabled together without layout glitches or main-thread stalls on large documents (visible-range updates only)
- [ ] Settings scene shows focus granularity and typewriter anchor options with tolerant load of older preference files
- [ ] Files saved before this change still load

title: #3 Atomic document save coordinator
description:
**Roadmap #:** 3 · **Scope:** M · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
Interrupted or failed saves must not lose user writing.

### Proposed behavior
Serialized per-document writes with temp-file replace, revision token, recoverable draft on failure; dirty state clears only on successful commit.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Editable local notes and recovery-oriented workflow (implementation details U).

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/DocumentStore.swift, SaveCoordinator.swift; Tests/SilkwebCoreTests/SaveCoordinatorTests.swift with injected filesystem failures.

### Constraints
Atomic write temp + replace; never lose text on failure paths.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `./scripts/build.sh` succeeds
- [ ] `./scripts/build.sh test` passes with new XCTest coverage for SaveCoordinatorTests with injected filesystem failures. logic
- [ ] Files saved before this change still load
- [ ] Simulated write/replace failure retains prior on-disk content and recoverable in-memory draft
- [ ] Concurrent saves for different documents do not corrupt each other
- [ ] Dirty flag clears only after successful atomic commit

title: #4 Three-pane library shell
description:
**Roadmap #:** 4 · **Scope:** M · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
The app cannot navigate a library yet.

### Proposed behavior
Library root chooser, folder outline, direct-child document list, selection plumbing, read-only document placeholder; keyboard tree navigation; clear empty and error states. Usable shell before editor integration.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Category sidebar, document list, editor area layout.

### Likely files
Sources/Silkweb/SilkwebApp.swift, LibraryWorkspace.swift, FolderSidebar.swift, DocumentList.swift.

### Constraints
Thin app layer; scan via Core APIs from #1.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `./scripts/build.sh` succeeds
- [ ] User can choose a library root and see folder tree plus direct documents for selected folder
- [ ] Keyboard navigation moves selection in the folder outline
- [ ] Empty library and load error states are shown without crashing

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.text: PRODUCT OWNER DECISION: first launch / no library offers both 'Open Folder in Place…' and 'New Library…'. Import Copy (silkweb-1.10) is a File menu command.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.text: ORCHESTRATOR FOLLOW-UP from silkweb-1.1 QA: LibraryScanner.scan always calls LibraryMetadataStore.save (LibraryScanner.swift:79), so a read-only or permission-restricted root throws. As part of 1.4, opening a read-only folder must still show the library (read-only state, clear banner copy, mutations disabled) and the scan must only write index.json when metadata actually changed. Add a Core test for the read-only root case.

title: #5 Native text editor with autosave
description:
**Roadmap #:** 5 · **Scope:** L · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
Users cannot write safely in the app.

### Proposed behavior
NSTextView bridge with Unicode/IME, undo/redo, plain-text paste, native spelling; debounced autosave and flush before selection change/close; save failures retain buffer and block silent loss.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Source-first Markdown editing with native Edit commands.

### Likely files
Sources/Silkweb/MarkdownTextView.swift, DocumentSession.swift, AppCommands.swift; Core tests for buffer/save scheduling where testable without AppKit.

### Constraints
Debounce saves; no main-thread library rescan per keystroke.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `./scripts/build.sh` succeeds
- [ ] `./scripts/build.sh test` passes with new XCTest coverage for save scheduling where testable without AppKit. logic
- [ ] Files saved before this change still load
- [ ] Editing a selected document persists UTF-8 content via save coordinator (#3)
- [ ] Plain-text paste does not inject rich formatting
- [ ] Failed save keeps editor buffer and surfaces error without discarding text

title: #6 Create and rename from the library
description:
**Roadmap #:** 6 · **Scope:** M · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
An empty library offers no writing entry point.

### Proposed behavior
New folder, subfolder, and document in selection context; inline/editable filename with validation; Finder reveal; save before rename; stable selection after rename.

### MWeb / competitor reference
New note/category and external-folder context commands.

### Likely files
Sources/Silkweb/LibraryCommands.swift, FolderSidebar.swift, DocumentList.swift.

### Constraints
Reject empty, reserved, separator, and colliding names per research contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `./scripts/build.sh` succeeds
- [ ] New document and folder commands create filesystem entries under selected parent
- [ ] Invalid names show validation feedback and do not touch disk
- [ ] Rename saves dirty document before renaming file; selection follows renamed item

title: #7 Folder and document moves with link planning
description:
**Roadmap #:** 7 · **Scope:** L · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
Folders and notes cannot be reorganized reliably.

### Proposed behavior
Internal drag/drop and Move To… share one transaction; prevent cycles and overwrites; preserve IDs; preflight supported relative Markdown link rewrites with staged rollback; report unsupported links.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Category drag management and external-folder tree (link-repair parity U).

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/MovePlan.swift, MarkdownDestinations.swift; Sources/Silkweb/MovePicker.swift; sidebar/list drop delegates.

### Constraints
Explicit bounded rewrite grammar; no silent merge on collision (cancel or unique name).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `./scripts/build.sh` succeeds
- [ ] `./scripts/build.sh test` passes with new XCTest coverage for list drop delegates. logic
- [ ] Files saved before this change still load
- [ ] Moving a folder moves descendants; cycle and root moves rejected
- [ ] Supported relative Markdown links update when source/target moves require it
- [ ] Dirty document is saved before move; failure rolls back filesystem and link staging
- [ ] Unsupported link syntax is preserved and listed, not silently broken

title: #8 Trash-based deletion
description:
**Roadmap #:** 8 · **Scope:** M · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
Deletion must be reversible.

### Proposed behavior
System Trash for documents and folders; descendant summary for nonempty folders; flush dirty state first; sensible selection after delete; no permanent-delete command.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Library Trash vs external system Trash (Silkweb: unified macOS Trash).

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/DeletionPlan.swift; Sources/Silkweb/TrashService.swift, LibraryCommands.swift.

### Constraints
Never silent permanent erasure.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `./scripts/build.sh` succeeds
- [ ] `./scripts/build.sh test` passes with new XCTest coverage for TrashService logic
- [ ] Delete moves items to macOS Trash (not immediate unlink)
- [ ] Nonempty folder delete explains descendant impact before confirming
- [ ] Dirty documents are saved or user is prompted before trashing

title: #9 Folder counts and document sorting
description:
**Roadmap #:** 9 · **Scope:** S · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
Users cannot scan or understand hierarchy size and document order.

### Proposed behavior
Direct document counts in sidebar; explicit include-subfolders recursive mode in list; natural folder ordering; name/created/modified sorts with stable tie-breakers; per-folder remembered sort preference.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Title/date/custom sorts (manual order excluded).

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/LibraryPresentation.swift; Sources/Silkweb/FolderSidebar.swift, DocumentList.swift.

### Constraints
Manual drag ordering deferred; disk filenames do not encode display order.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `./scripts/build.sh` succeeds
- [ ] `./scripts/build.sh test` passes with new XCTest coverage for FolderSidebar logic
- [ ] Files saved before this change still load
- [ ] Sidebar shows direct child document counts by default
- [ ] List supports name, created, and modified ascending/descending with deterministic ties
- [ ] Include Subfolders toggles recursive document listing
